minutes.headline: Heard Monty Tech's FY21 budget showing a big jump in Lunenburg's assessment; new growth estimate is low
minutes.summary: The committee heard the public access committee's budget, then Monty Tech's superintendent and business manager on the FY21 budget and a higher Lunenburg assessment driven by the state formula and more students. The assessor explained why new growth is down and how values were raised. Two sets of minutes were approved and the March schedule and warrant items were discussed.

what_happened.line: Monty Tech's superintendent and business manager presented the FY21 budget, including a higher required Lunenburg contribution tied to the state formula and seven more students.
The updated town budget moved money to the schools line after the Monty Tech change, leaving a smaller unallocated balance.
The assessor said new growth is expected to hold at about a floor each year, but the current estimate is low.
The committee heard the public access budget, funded from cable franchise fees rather than the general fund.

The committee will try to hold a Monday March 23 meeting before the public hearing to prepare the warrant letter, and asked the Board of Selectmen to help invite the senator and representative on school funding.

why_it_matters: Lunenburg's Monty Tech assessment is set by a state formula and enrollment, so it can rise even when the school's overall budget is nearly flat, and it draws on the same town budget that funds other services.
Low new growth means less added tax revenue without raising the rate, which narrows what the town budget can absorb.
